capital-one-platinum-secured.name: Capital One Platinum Secured
capital-one-platinum-secured.h1: A real card from a major bank — for the price of a pizza night.
capital-one-platinum-secured.hero: The Capital One Platinum Secured starts with a deposit as low as $49 — the lowest among major issuers — with no annual fee and a path to an unsecured card.
capital-one-platinum-secured.depNote: Refundable deposit becomes your credit line

hook: Getting rejected because of a thin credit file stings twice: once by the denial, and again by every bank that sees it afterward. Capital One built the Platinum Secured precisely for that moment — for people who are new to credit or rebuilding after mistakes, and who cannot put hundreds of dollars on the table to prove themselves.

Most secured cards want $200 or more upfront. Capital One lowers that bar: your initial credit line can start at $49, $99, or $200 depending on your approval — you find out the exact amount before you commit a cent. No annual fee means the card costs you nothing while it quietly builds your file.
body.how: The mechanics are simple. You place a refundable security deposit with Capital One — that deposit becomes your credit line, not a fee. You use the card for small purchases, pay on time, and Capital One reports those payments to all three bureaus. After your first six months, Capital One reviews your account and may raise your credit line without an additional deposit. Responsible use over time can lead to graduation to an unsecured card and your deposit returned.
fit: New to credit with no score yet
Rebuilding after past mistakes
Can put aside $49–$200 as a one-time deposit
Want a major-bank card, not a subprime issuer
nofit: You need rewards from day one (look at the Quicksilver Secured)
You have no bank account at all (OpenSky works without one)
You want a card today with zero deposit (Credit One, with its annual fee)
body.compare: Compared with the Discover it® Secured, the Capital One path starts cheaper ($49 vs $200) but earns no rewards and has no automatic upgrade guarantee — Discover reviews at 7 months and converts strong accounts. Choose Capital One for the lowest entry cost; choose Discover when you can fund $200 and want cash back plus graduation.

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?

There is no hard credit pull to find out your pre-qualification. A full application does involve a credit check by the issuer, but for a secured card approval odds are not score-driven the way unsecured cards are.
What credit score do I need?

Capital One does not publish a minimum score for this card — it is designed for people with no score, limited history, or rebuilding credit. Your deposit and ability to fund it matter more than your score.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?

Payments are reported to all three bureaus from your first billing cycle. Many builders see measurable score movement after 3–6 months of on-time reporting; Capital One reviews your line for increase after 6 months.
What happens to my deposit?
It stays in a secured account and becomes your credit line — it is not a fee. If you upgrade to unsecured or close the account in good standing, the deposit is refunded.
Can I be denied?
Yes — secured does not mean guaranteed. Common denial reasons: insufficient income, unresolved delinquencies, or too many recent applications. You keep your deposit if you are denied before funding.

quicksilver-secured.name: Capital One Quicksilver Secured
quicksilver-secured.h1: Cash back while you rebuild — not either-or.
quicksilver-secured.hero: The Quicksilver Secured pays 1.5% cash back on everything while you build credit — unusual for a secured card, with a $200 refundable deposit and no annual fee.
quicksilver-secured.depNote: Refundable deposit becomes your credit line

hook: For years the rule was simple: secured cards build credit, rewards cards pay you. You picked one. Capital One broke the rule — the Quicksilver Secured pays unlimited 1.5% cash back on every purchase while your file grows underneath it.
If you are rebuilding, every dollar of spending you already do — gas, groceries, subscriptions — can work twice: once as the payment history that raises your score, once as cash back in your pocket.
body.how: You fund a $200 refundable deposit, which becomes your credit line. From the first swipe, purchases earn 1.5% cash back with no categories to track and no annual fee. Payments report to all three bureaus. Over time, Capital One reviews accounts for credit line increases and potential graduation to the unsecured Quicksilver — where the rewards structure continues.
fit: Rebuilding with regular monthly spending
Can fund a $200 deposit
Want rewards while building, not after
nofit: Cannot put $200 aside (Capital One Platinum Secured starts at $49)
No score at all and no bank account (OpenSky)
Maximum upgrade speed (Discover has auto reviews at 7 months)
body.compare: Versus the Discover it® Secured: Discover pays 2% at gas and restaurants (rotating first year double) and reviews automatically at 7 months, but needs the same $200 and solid on-time history. Quicksilver wins on simplicity — flat 1.5% everywhere, no activation needed.

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?
Pre-qualification uses a soft check with no score impact. A formal application involves a credit check, but as a secured card, approval centers on your deposit rather than your score.
What credit score do I need?
No published minimum — it targets fair, limited, or rebuilding credit. The $200 deposit is the real requirement.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
Reporting starts with your first billing cycle. Expect meaningful movement after 3–6 months; Capital One periodically reviews accounts for upgrades.
What happens to my deposit?
Refundable — it becomes your credit line. On graduation to unsecured or closure in good standing, you get it back.
Can I be denied?
Yes. Denied applications typically involve insufficient income, recent delinquencies, or application volume. Pre-qualifying first avoids surprises.

discover-it-secured.name: Discover it® Secured
discover-it-secured.h1: The secured card that graduates you — automatically.
discover-it-secured.hero: Discover reviews your account automatically starting at 7 months and converts strong accounts to unsecured — with your deposit back. Plus 2% cash back at gas stations and restaurants.

hook: The dirty secret of secured cards: many issuers are happy to keep your deposit forever. Discover designed the it® Secured to end — automatic reviews begin at 7 months, and cardholders in good standing graduate to unsecured with their deposit refunded.
That graduation path changes the psychology of rebuilding. You are not renting a credit line; you are on a timed track out of it.
body.how: Fund a $200 minimum refundable deposit. Spend and pay on time — Discover reports to all three bureaus. You earn 2% cash back at gas stations and restaurants (on up to $1,000 in combined purchases per quarter) and 1% on everything else, with all cash back matched at the end of your first year. Starting at 7 months, Discover reviews your account automatically; graduation depends on on-time payments and spending, not a score cutoff you have to guess.
fit: Rebuilding with steady income and on-time habits
Can fund $200 and keep utilization low
Want the clearest, most automatic graduation path
nofit: Cannot fund $200 yet (Capital One from $49)
No bank account (OpenSky)
Active bankruptcy (OpenSky is more forgiving)
body.compare: Versus Capital One Platinum Secured: Discover requires double the deposit but pays rewards and reviews automatically; Capital One starts cheaper with no rewards and no guaranteed upgrade timeline. If graduation is the priority, Discover is the strongest path in the category.

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?
Pre-qualification is a soft check. Applying triggers a hard inquiry, but Discover evaluates secured applications with rebuilding applicants in mind rather than score-minimums.
What credit score do I need?
No published minimum. This card accepts limited, fair, and rebuilding credit — the deposit and income matter most.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
Reporting begins with the first cycle; many see score movement in 3–6 months. Graduation reviews start at 7 months and continue periodically.
What happens to my deposit?
Refunded when you graduate to unsecured or close in good standing — that is the design goal of the product.
Can I be denied?
Yes — especially with unresolved delinquencies or excessive recent applications. Discover offers pre-qualification to check first.

opensky-secured.name: OpenSky® Secured Visa®
opensky-secured.h1: After bankruptcy, when most banks close the door.
opensky-secured.hero: OpenSky approves without a credit check, considers applicants in active or discharged bankruptcy, and needs no bank account — $100 minimum deposit.
opensky-secured.depNote: Refundable deposit becomes your credit line

hook: A bankruptcy filing closes most credit doors for years. OpenSky exists for exactly that moment: no credit check to apply, and issuers' usual bankruptcy exclusions do not apply here — applicants with active or discharged bankruptcies are considered.
That makes OpenSky the most common second-chance card in rebuild-after-setback journeys — not the cheapest, but the one most likely to say yes.
body.how: You fund a refundable deposit between $100 and $3,000 — it becomes your credit line. No credit check is performed. Payments report to all three bureaus from the start. The $35 annual fee is the trade-off for the flexible approval; there is no interest as long as you pay your statement balance. Upgrade to unsecured is possible after a history of on-time payments.
fit: Active or discharged bankruptcy
No bank account (fund by money order or debit)
Denied by major issuers repeatedly
nofit: Want $0 annual fee (Chime, if a checking account fits you)
Want rewards (Quicksilver Secured)
Have fair credit and no bankruptcy history (better options exist)
body.compare: Versus the Self Secured Visa: Self requires no cash upfront (it builds through a credit-builder loan), which suits tighter budgets; OpenSky is faster to a usable credit line and more established for bankruptcy cases. Versus Chime: Chime has no fee but requires a checking account with direct deposit.

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?
No — OpenSky performs no credit check at application. Approval is based on your deposit and identity verification.
What credit score do I need?
None. There is no score requirement, and bankruptcy does not disqualify you — the deposit is the collateral.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
Reporting starts with your first cycle. With bankruptcy on file, expect a longer arc — 6–12 months of on-time reporting before meaningful movement.
What happens to my deposit?
It is refundable — returned if you close in good standing or upgrade to unsecured.
Can I be denied?
Rarely, but yes — identity verification failure, deposit funding failure, or application volume can lead to denial.

opensky-no-bank-account.name: OpenSky® Secured Visa®
opensky-no-bank-account.h1: No bank account? No problem — that's the point.
opensky-no-bank-account.hero: OpenSky is one of the few cards that requires no checking account at all — fund your refundable deposit by money order or debit card and start building.
opensky-no-bank-account.depNote: Refundable deposit becomes your credit line

hook: An estimated 4.5% of US households are unbanked — no checking account, no direct deposit, no relationship with a bank. Nearly every credit builder card quietly assumes you have one. OpenSky does not.

Whether you left traditional banking by choice or circumstance, OpenSky lets you fund a refundable deposit by money order, debit card, or bank transfer — no account required to apply or to keep the card.
body.how: Choose a deposit between $100 and $3,000 — it becomes your credit line and is fully refundable. No credit check, no bank account, no Chime-style direct deposit requirements. Payments report to all three bureaus. Manage the account online or by phone; the $35 annual fee covers the flexibility.
fit: No checking account, by choice or circumstance
Prefer not to link bank credentials anywhere
Rebuilding with cash-based finances
nofit: Want a $0-fee option and have a bank account (Chime)
Want rewards (Quicksilver Secured)
Have $0 to deposit (Self builds via loan instead)

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?
No credit check is performed — application does not touch your score.
What credit score do I need?
None. Deposit and identity verification decide approval.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
First-cycle reporting; typical builders see movement within 3–6 months of on-time payments.

Refundable at closure in good standing or upgrade.

Yes, mainly for identity or funding verification issues — not for score or banking history.

credit-one-platinum.name: Credit One Platinum
credit-one-platinum.h1: No deposit, no collateral — at a price you should see coming.
credit-one-platinum.hero: Credit One Platinum is unsecured — no deposit — designed for fair-to-building credit. It carries an annual fee ($75–99) that we show up front, because surprises are the enemy of rebuilding.

hook: Every secured card asks the same thing: cash upfront. If you have $0 to spare, that is a wall. Credit One Platinum removes it — no deposit, unsecured, aimed at fair or rebuilding credit.

The trade is honesty about a fee: $75 in year one, then $99 annually (billed $8.25 monthly). For some rebuilders that fee is worth skipping the deposit; for others it is exactly why the secured path wins. We show both sides because trust beats a surprise statement.
body.how: There is no deposit to fund. You apply, Credit One checks your credit, and if approved you get a modest unsecured line — often starting around $300–$500. Payments report to all three major bureaus. Cash back (1% on eligible purchases) applies on some versions of this card; check your offer terms.
fit: Zero dollars available for a deposit
Fair credit with some history
Value unsecured over low cost
nofit: Can fund $49+ — the Capital One Platinum Secured is fee-free and cheaper long-term
No score and no bank account (OpenSky)
Active bankruptcy (OpenSky again)
body.compare: Versus Capital One Platinum Secured: Credit One needs no deposit but costs $75–99/year forever; Capital One needs a refundable deposit and costs $0/year. Over two years, the secured path saves $150–198 and returns the deposit. Choose Credit One only when the deposit is truly impossible.

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?
Applying involves a hard credit check — there is no soft pre-qualification for this product. One application, one inquiry.
What credit score do I need?
Targeted at fair credit (roughly 580–669 range, though no official minimum is published). Poor or no credit usually needs the secured or no-credit-check routes.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
Reporting begins with the first cycle; movement typically appears within 3–6 months of on-time payments.
What happens to my deposit?
There is no deposit — this card is unsecured. The cost is the annual fee instead.
Can I be denied?
Yes — this is a real unsecured approval with hard-pull underwriting, so denial rates are meaningfully higher than secured options.

indigo-mastercard.name: Indigo® Mastercard®
indigo-mastercard.h1: See your odds before you apply — no hard pull.
indigo-mastercard.hero: Indigo offers pre-qualification with no hard credit pull — check whether you are likely approved before any inquiry hits your file.
indigo-mastercard.warn: Annual fee $0 first year, then $75+ (varies by offer)

hook: The scariest part of rebuilding is not denial — it is another hard inquiry on a file that cannot afford one. Indigo's pre-qualification answers the question first: see whether you are likely approved, with no score impact, before you decide.
For people who have been burned by repeated applications, that order of operations — check, then apply — is the whole value proposition.
body.how: Start with pre-qualification: a soft check that does not affect your score. If the odds look good, complete the application (that step does involve a hard pull). The card is unsecured with no deposit; annual fee depends on the offer you are pre-qualified for — some are $0 the first year, others carry $75+ thereafter. Payments report to all three bureaus.

Fair or rebuilding credit with some history
Prefer unsecured over deposit

No score at all (no-credit-check secured cards fit better)
Want rewards (Quicksilver Secured)

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?
Pre-qualification is a soft pull — no impact. Completing a full application does involve a hard inquiry.
What credit score do I need?
Designed for fair to rebuilding credit; the pre-qualification tells you where you stand before applying.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
Reporting starts with the first cycle; typical movement within 3–6 months of on-time payments.
What happens to my deposit?
No deposit — this card is unsecured. Costs come from the annual fee structure of your offer.
Can I be denied?
Yes, even after pre-qualification — pre-qual is directional, not a guarantee. Final approval depends on the full underwriting check.

self-secured-visa.name: Self Secured Visa®
self-secured-visa.h1: Build credit without cash upfront — the loan does the deposit.
self-secured-visa.hero: The Self Secured Visa uses your Self Credit Builder Account as the security deposit — no extra cash needed to start building with a real card.
self-secured-visa.depNote: Funded by your Credit Builder Account savings

hook: The cruelest joke in credit building: the cards that help you the most demand money you do not have. Self solved it by joining two products — the credit-builder loan you may already be paying into becomes the security deposit for a real Visa card.
No lump sum. No new savings goal. The building blocks you set up for your score become the collateral for spending power.
body.how: If you have (or open) a Self Credit Builder Account, once you accumulate $100 or more in savings progress, you can unlock the Secured Visa against it — no additional deposit. Payments report to all three bureaus. You manage spending against your loan savings; the $25 annual fee is modest, and the account doubles as a forced-savings mechanism.
fit: No cash for a deposit right now
Already in (or open to) a credit-builder loan
Want savings discipline alongside credit building
nofit: Want a full credit line immediately (secured deposits give bigger lines)
Already have $200+ to deposit (Discover/CapOne offer rewards or free paths)
Do not want any loan product
body.compare: Versus OpenSky: OpenSky needs $100+ cash but no loan relationship and handles bankruptcy cases more directly; Self needs no cash but requires the loan structure. For $0-upfront rebuilding, Self is the cleanest hybrid.

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?

Checking eligibility inside your Self account is a soft process; the card application itself may involve a credit check. The Credit Builder Account itself reports as an installment loan — a score positive over time.
What credit score do I need?
The loan plus card structure is designed for no-score and rebuilding profiles — eligibility is driven by your Self account progress, not a score minimum.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
You are building two ways at once — installment loan plus card payments. Expect visible movement in 3–6 months of on-time activity.
What happens to my deposit?
It is your own loan savings — at loan completion the money is yours, minus fees.
Can I be denied?
Yes — mainly if your Self account is too new or progress is below the threshold.

upgrade-card.name: Upgrade Card
upgrade-card.h1: A card that behaves like a loan — fixed payments, no surprises.
upgrade-card.hero: The Upgrade Card turns your balance into fixed-installment payments — build credit through predictable monthly payments instead of revolving debt.

hook: Revolving credit is where rebuilders get hurt: a balance that lingers, interest that snowballs, a score that dips with utilization. The Upgrade Card redesigns the mechanics — every balance you carry becomes a fixed-payment installment plan, reported as personal loans, not revolving debt.
For people who got into trouble precisely because credit cards are too flexible, the rigidity is the feature.
body.how: Apply once; if approved you get a line you draw against. Each draw becomes an installment with fixed monthly payments and a fixed payoff date. On-time payments report to all three bureaus. There is no annual fee; APR depends on your credit profile at approval. Because utilization on the card does not swing your score the way revolving balances do, the score path is calmer.
fit: Prefer fixed payments over revolving flexibility
Rebuilding with steady income
Want credit-building without deposit
nofit: Want traditional swipe-anywhere rewards (Quicksilver Secured)
No score and no income (secured no-check options first)
Active bankruptcy (OpenSky)
body.compare: Versus the Self Secured Visa: both add installment-style reporting, but Upgrade gives you spending power now with no savings account; Self builds savings first. Upgrade suits earners; Self suits savers-in-training.

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?
Checking your offer uses a soft pull. Accepting and drawing involves a hard inquiry for most applicants.
What credit score do I need?
Upgrade targets fair-and-better profiles (roughly 560+ in practice). Poor/no credit usually starts with secured or no-check products.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
Installment history builds steadily — expect measurable impact over 6+ months of on-time payments.
What happens to my deposit?
There is no deposit — the product is unsecured with fixed installment draws.
Can I be denied?
Yes — underwriting is income- and history-based, stricter than no-check secured cards.

fast-credit-limit-increase.name: Fast Credit Limit Increase — Which Card Grows Quickest
fast-credit-limit-increase.h1: Which secured card raises your limit fastest (and why it matters).
fast-credit-limit-increase.hero: Credit line growth is the quiet lever of credit building — lower utilization, higher scores. Here is how fast each major secured card actually grows.

hook: Two builders pay on time every month. Six months later one has a $2,000 limit and a 760 score; the other is stuck at $200 and 640. The difference is not discipline — it is which card they picked, because issuers grow limits at very different speeds.
Utilization (balance ÷ limit) is roughly 30% of your score. A $50 balance is 25% of a $200 line but 3% of a $1,700 line. Same spending, wildly different score math.
body.how: Three growth patterns matter. (1) Capital One Platinum Secured: after 6 months of on-time payments, Capital One reviews and may add line without extra deposit — the fastest no-effort grower. (2) Discover it Secured: automatic reviews begin at 7 months and can graduate you to unsecured entirely, returning your deposit. (3) OpenSky and similar subprime issuers: manual requests, slower growth, or none — you get what you fund.
fit: Choosing between secured cards by growth speed
Already have a secured card and want a raise
Planning the rebuild arc end-to-end
nofit: Looking for rewards comparison (see our zero-fee guide)
No card yet and no deposit (start with the quiz)
body.compare: Fastest no-effort growth: Capital One (6-month review). Fastest exit to unsecured: Discover (7-month reviews). Slowest: subprime issuers with manual-only increases. The meta-lesson: pick the issuer whose growth pattern matches your timeline.

faq: Does asking for a credit limit increase hurt my score?
Some issuers run a hard pull for CLI requests; automatic reviews do not. Capital One and Discover automatic reviews are soft — no score impact.
What credit score do I need?
CLI approvals track your payment history on the card more than your score — 6 months of on-time payments is the real threshold.
How long does it take to build credit with a higher limit?
Utilization improves immediately when a limit rises; the score effect typically shows in the next reporting cycle.
What happens to my deposit when my limit grows?
On secured cards, either you fund the increase (deposit grows) or the issuer adds unsecured line on top — Discover and Capital One do the latter on strong accounts.
Can I be denied a limit increase?
Yes — late payments, high utilization, or a too-new account all lead to denials. Wait for the automatic review.

discover-student.name: Discover it® Student
discover-student.h1: Student? This is the rare card that says yes without a history.
discover-student.hero: The Discover it® Student accepts limited credit with student-friendly underwriting — 5% rotating cash back, no annual fee, and a free FICO score in the app.

hook: Students face a paradox: no card means no history, no history means no card. Issuer student cards break the loop by underwriting on enrollment and income rather than score — and Discover's student card is the most generous of the category: real rewards, no annual fee, and a score tracker built in.
Start in college and you graduate with 4+ years of payment history — the single largest score factor — already banked.
body.how: Apply with proof of enrollment and some income (scholarships and part-time work count). If approved, you get an unsecured line with 5% cash back in rotating quarterly categories (activation required) and 1% on everything else — first-year cash back matched automatically. No annual fee, no penalty APR on the first late payment (a genuinely useful grace for first-time cardholders), and free FICO score monitoring.
fit: Enrolled student with any income source
First credit card ever
Want rewards without a deposit
nofit: Not enrolled (secured cards are the path)
Want a flat rate with no category tracking (Quicksilver-style)
Rebuilding with negatives (student underwriting is for clean thin files)
body.compare: Versus the Chime Credit Builder: Chime is easier to get (no check) but builds no rewards and needs the checking account. The student card pays more and costs nothing, but requires enrollment — graduation from student status means applying again for a standard card.

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?
Pre-qualification is available with a soft check. Applying involves a hard inquiry — but for students, a single inquiry at the start of a long file is a small cost.
What credit score do I need?
There is no published minimum — underwriting weighs enrollment and income. Many approvals happen with no score at all.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
First-cycle reporting. Students who start freshman year typically graduate with strong prime-ready files.
What happens to my deposit?
No deposit — unsecured. The card may upgrade or convert as your profile matures.
Can I be denied?
Yes — typically for insufficient income or enrollment verification failure.

chime-credit-builder.name: Chime Credit Builder
chime-credit-builder.h1: No history? No problem. No fee, either.
chime-credit-builder.hero: The Chime Credit Builder Visa® has no annual fee, no credit check to apply, and reports to all three bureaus — the simplest way to start a score from zero.
chime-credit-builder.depNote: You move your own money to the card as you spend

hook: Starting from zero is its own kind of trap: no card means no history, and no history means most issuers will not look at you twice. The Chime Credit Builder was designed for exactly that door — no credit check to apply, no annual fee, and a spend-only design that makes overspending impossible.

Instead of a deposit that sits locked, Chime moves money from your Chime checking account to the card as you spend it. There is no interest and no balance to carry — the card can only spend what you moved. Payments report to all three bureaus like any card, which is where the score comes from.
body.how: Open a Chime checking account with a qualifying direct deposit, then request the Credit Builder card in the app — no credit check involved. Move money into the Credit Builder account when you want spending power; the card draws only from that. Each swipe is reported as a payment (because you are effectively paying as you go), and on-time reporting builds the file. Turn on AutoPay in the app so the reporting never slips.
fit: No credit history at all
Want a $0-fee start with zero overspend risk
Have (or will open) a Chime checking account
nofit: Do not want a bank account (OpenSky works without one)
Want rewards immediately (Quicksilver Secured)
Need a large credit line fast (secured deposits give bigger lines)

Chime wins on total cost and safety; Capital One wins on line size and graduation path.

faq: Does this card hurt my credit score?
There is no credit check to apply, so no hard inquiry. Missed payments would be reported — AutoPay prevents that.
What credit score do I need?
None. Approval does not depend on score — only a Chime checking account with qualifying direct deposit.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
Payment history is the largest score factor; many builders see movement after 3–6 months of on-time reporting.
What happens to my deposit?
There is no locked deposit — you move your own money to the card as you spend, so it stays yours throughout.
Can I be denied?
Yes, mainly if the checking account or direct deposit requirements are not met — not for score reasons.

secured-vs-credit-builder-loan.h1: Secured card or credit-builder loan — which builds faster?
secured-vs-credit-builder-loan.hero: Both build credit without a traditional card approval. They work on different mechanics, cost different amounts, and suit different situations. Here is the honest comparison.

hook: You know you need credit history. You do not know which tool to start with. Secured cards and credit-builder loans are the two standard answers — and they are not interchangeable.

A secured card gives you spending power immediately and builds revolving history — the category most of your score cares about. A credit-builder loan locks your money in a savings account and reports installment history — no spending temptation, but no spending power either.
body.how: Secured card: fund a refundable deposit ($49–$200 typically), spend small, pay in full — revolving history reports monthly. Credit-builder loan: the lender places your loan amount in a locked savings account; you pay fixed monthly installments for 12–24 months, then receive the savings — installment history reports monthly. The Self Secured Visa merges both: your loan savings become a card deposit.
fit: Card: you have $49–$200 and want spending power
Loan: you cannot risk overspending while rebuilding
Self hybrid: you want both without choosing
nofit: Card: you have $0 and no discipline risk — wait, that is the loan's job
Loan: you need a card for deposits, hotels, car rentals now
body.compare: Score mechanics differ: revolving utilization vs installment mix. Ideally you eventually have both — the loan adds account-mix (10% of score) while the card builds the core payment history. Cost: secured cards with $0 fee (Chime, Capital One) beat loan interest/fees; loans win on forced savings.
body.pitfalls: If you can only pick one today, pick by risk profile rather than by score math: if overspending is what damaged your credit, the loan's locked structure protects you from yourself while history accumulates; if your spending is already disciplined, the card starts building the revolving category immediately and gives you spending utility. The hybrid (Self) exists precisely because many rebuilders want both and can only afford one payment stream. Cost comparison over 24 months: a $0-fee secured card costs $0 (deposit returned); a typical credit-builder loan costs $25–90 in fees/interest over its life; a $0-deposit unsecured card (Credit One, Indigo) costs $150–198. Cheapest is not always fastest — but fastest is rarely free.
body.steps: Practical next step: check your current file before choosing. If you have zero accounts reporting, the loan adds an installment line to an empty report (diversity from day one). If one card already reports, the loan adds mix while a second card mostly deepens utilization headroom. The quiz routes on exactly this distinction.

faq: Does checking or applying hurt my credit score?
Secured card pre-qualification is soft; loan applications vary — Self and most credit-builder lenders use soft checks for approval.
What credit score do I need?
Neither product requires a minimum score — both exist for no-score and rebuilding profiles.
How long does it take to build credit with this card?
Both report monthly from the first cycle; expect meaningful movement in 3–6 months.
What happens to my deposit?
Secured card deposits refund on upgrade or closure in good standing; loan "deposits" are your own savings returned at completion.
Can I be denied?
Yes for cards (identity, income); credit-builder loans have the highest approval rates of any credit product.

best-zero-fee-secured-cards.hero: Five secured cards cost you nothing per year. We rank them by real value — graduation path, deposit size, and what they actually report.

hook: A $0 annual fee is not automatically a good deal — some free secured cards trap your deposit for years with no graduation path. The real ranking weighs three things: what the card costs (nothing), when you get out (graduation speed), and what it reports (all three bureaus, always).
After those filters, the field narrows to a handful of genuine options.
body.how: Our ranking: (1) Discover it Secured — $0 fee, 2% category cash back, auto graduation reviews at 7 months, deposit back on conversion. (2) Capital One Platinum Secured — $0 fee, deposit from $49, 6-month line reviews. (3) Chime Credit Builder — $0 fee, no credit check, but requires the Chime checking account. (4) Capital One Quicksilver Secured — $0 fee, 1.5% back, $200 deposit. (5) OpenSky — $35 fee, included only because it serves no-bank and bankruptcy cases the others reject.
fit: Anyone comparing secured cards by total cost
Rebuilders optimizing for graduation, not just approval
nofit: Need no-bank-account or bankruptcy-friendly approval (OpenSky, despite the fee)
Have $0 deposit (Self or Credit One — different fee structures)
body.compare: The fee trap to avoid: subprime unsecured cards advertising "no deposit" with $75–99 annual fees (Credit One, Indigo) cost $150–198 over two years — more than every card on this list. The deposit path returns its money; the fee path does not.
body.pitfalls: The one trap this ranking guards against: cards that advertise "$0 deposit" or "guaranteed" while charging $75–99 annually. Over a two-year rebuild, those fees total $150–198 — more than every card on this list costs combined. The deposit path costs nothing at graduation; the fee path never returns a cent. Another quiet differentiator: reporting completeness. All five cards report to all three bureaus, but Chime's spend-only design reports payments differently — the score effect is equivalent, but utilization modeling differs because there is no fixed line.
body.steps: Practical next step: run the numbers on your own rebuild — total cost = (annual fee × years) + (deposit you cannot touch). A card that looks expensive per month but returns its deposit at graduation usually wins the two-year math. The quiz applies these same criteria to your deposit budget automatically.

secured-cards-under-100-deposit.h1: Secured cards under $100 deposit — the real list.
secured-cards-under-100-deposit.hero: Most secured cards want $200. Four genuine options start below $100 — here is what each trade costs you.

hook: The $200 minimum is the most common wall in credit rebuilding. Below $100, the options narrow fast — and one of them is not what it appears. Here is the honest list of cards that start under $100.
Spoiler: the cheapest deposit is rarely the cheapest card.
body.how: The list: (1) Capital One Platinum Secured — deposit from $49 (Capital One assigns $49/$99/$200 by approval); $0 annual fee; no rewards; 6-month line reviews. (2) Chime Credit Builder — $0 deposit (you move money as you spend); requires the Chime checking account; no credit check. (3) OpenSky — $100 minimum (right at the line); $35 fee; no credit check, bankruptcy-friendly. (4) Self Secured Visa — no cash deposit (loan-funded); requires the Credit Builder Account.
fit: Budgets under $100 for one-time deposit
No bank account (OpenSky) or no cash (Self/Chime)
First-ever card
nofit: Want rewards — under-$100 options skip rewards by design
Want big credit lines immediately (deposit size = line size)
body.compare: Capital One is the best pure value under $100 ($0 fee, major bank). Chime wins for zero total cost if the checking account works for you. OpenSky is the fallback when the first two doors close. Avoid "low deposit" offers from subprime issuers with annual fees — the fee eats the deposit advantage within a year.
body.pitfalls: A practical warning: "low deposit" offers from subprime issuers usually hide annual fees that erase the deposit advantage within the first year. If a card under $100 deposit carries a $75+ fee, the math is worse than saving another month to fund a $0-fee option. Also worth knowing: deposit size equals credit line, so a $49 line means a $15 grocery run is 30% utilization. Two mitigations exist — pay before the statement date (the reported balance is what matters), or grow the line via Capital One's 6-month review. Budget builders should treat the first deposit as a floor, not a ceiling.
body.steps: Practical next step: if your budget is fixed under $100, decide which constraint binds first — the deposit itself, the bank account requirement, or the annual fee. Each of the four cards above removes exactly one constraint; matching your binding constraint to the right card matters more than any feature comparison.
